authors: Preet P. S. Saluja, David J. Jobe, Jacques C. LeBlanc, Robert J. Lemire
journal: Journal of Chemical and Engineering Data 40(2), 398-406
title: Apparent Molar Heat Capacities and Volumes of Mixed Electrolytes: [NaCl(aq) + CaCl2(aq)], [NaCl(aq) + MgCl2(aq)], and [CaCl2(aq) + MgCl2(aq)]
experimental_method: Flow differential heat capacity microcalorimeter in series with a vibrating-tube densimeter, 298.15 to 373.15 K at 0.6 MPa, solutions prepared by weight.
uncertainties_stated: Temperature stable to +-0.003 K, accuracy +-0.05 K; pressure +-50 kPa; precision in cp +-4 mJ/(K g); density +-1e-5 g/cm3; concentrations (chloride analyses) +-0.5%.
quality_remarks: Table 1 and Table 4 give the measured volume heat-capacity ratio and density difference together with apparent molar quantities calculated by the authors (derived_by_authors). Density temperature differs from the heat-capacity temperature (e.g. 297.05 K vs 298.15 K in Table 1; 296.02 K in Table 4). Concentration of MgCl2 and CaCl2 based on chloride analysis of hydrates. Some of the MgCl2 and CaCl2 binary values were reported previously (Saluja and LeBlanc 1987) according to the text; the table here includes all printed values.
